## 3. The evidence that moved it










**A spatial unit, not a cell type, is what immunotherapy requires.**
[38906155](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38906155/) (*Cancer Cell*): intratumoral immune **triads** are required for
immunotherapy-mediated elimination of solid tumours. The operative requirement is
a multicellular arrangement. Read against the whole
`suppressive-population-inversion` thread, this is the constructive version of
the same objection: if the functional unit is a triad, then depleting or blocking
any single population in it has an unpredictable sign, which is exactly what the
inversion cards keep reporting.

**Resistance that costs the cell its tumour.** [38533987](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38533987/) (*Cancer Discov*)
inhibits protein phosphatase 2A in colon cancer cells, which hyperactivates
several oncogenic pathways at once and engages the stress responses that
aberrant signalling provokes. Genetic and compound screens find combined PP2A and
WEE1 inhibition synergistic across models: replication collapses, mitosis comes
early, the cells die, and patient-derived tumours shrink in vivo. The part worth
keeping is the resistance phenotype — cells that acquire resistance to the
combination lose oncogenic signalling and with it the ability to form tumours at
all. Tumour-suppressive drug resistance is a genuinely unusual object and it
belongs to no thread here.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    Three errors came out of this one title. The entry read: "The sign of an
    intervention is treated as an open question in a review-of-record venue — a
    year before the corpus starts logging sign reversals as a pattern." The
    record is not a commentary but a primary research article with genetic and
    compound screens and PDX work, so there is no review-of-record venue treating
    anything as open. It was carded on `next-gen-checkpoints`, and contains no
    checkpoint, no immune target and no antibody. And the gloss about the sign of
    an intervention has no counterpart in the paper. The card is now `neutral`,
    typed `mechanism`, and carries no thread.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Nothing lands on a tracked thread this month.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This section carried [38969522](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38969522/) (*JITC*): "infliximab in
    steroid-refractory immune-related hepatitis does not demonstrate
    hepatotoxicity and may shorten time on steroids — a feared toxicity that does
    not appear." The finding is real — a ten-patient single-centre retrospective
    series in which infliximab controlled grade ≥3 immune-related hepatitis in 7
    of 10 without liver injury, resolved in 9 of 10 at a median 487 days — but it
    is the management of an immune-related adverse event, not a mechanism of
    checkpoint resistance, and it was carded `supports` on
    `immunotherapy-resistance`. None of the other thirty cards on that thread is
    about toxicity. The card keeps the finding, is now `neutral`, and has no
    thread in this corpus.

### (b) Method credibility

Three concern-and-retraction notices in one month, but two fewer signals than
that count suggests. [38946327](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38946327/) and [38946326](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38946326/) (*Cancer Discov*) are
Expressions of Concern on drug-addiction-based selection against MAPKi-resistant
melanoma and on durable suppression of acquired MEK-inhibitor resistance. The
papers are distinct and both notices stay on the ledger, but they share their
first author and come out of one laboratory's body of work, so they are one
investigation reaching two papers rather than two investigations. [38870944](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38870944/)
(*Cell*, retraction of a genomic decoding of neuronal depolarisation) is separate.
Both *Cancer Discovery* notices attach to resistance-mechanism papers, which is
the literature the `immunotherapy-resistance` thread draws on.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    The old phrasing — "two of them in the same journal", "the second concern
    notice in the same journal and month" — presented the pair as an independent
    second signal. Same journal, same month, therefore separate sources is the
    inference that also failed on the two pathology foundation models in March,
    in the other direction.

[39030569](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39030569/) (*Genome Biol*) benchmarks methods for correcting biases of
established **and unknown** origin in CRISPR-Cas9 screening data — the unknown
half is the admission.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    [38951922](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38951922/) was in this paragraph, described as evaluating
    variant-effect predictors "by their ability to infer human traits rather than
    against curated labels, which is the same move as the 2026
    sequence-to-function evaluations against real inter-individual variation".
    The method is as described — 24 predictors scored against rare-variant trait
    associations in UK Biobank and All of Us, which sidesteps the circularity of
    testing against training labels — but nothing in it is found unreliable.
    AlphaMissense outperforms the rest in both cohorts and the two rankings agree.
    A benchmark with no adverse finding is not an entry in a ledger of things
    found unreliable, and this corpus already cards that genre `neutral`
    elsewhere. The stance is now `neutral`; the reading forward to 2026 was
    hindsight and is withdrawn with it.
